cases.justification: The implement role resolves to its declared primary (nim) then its two declared free fallbacks, in declared order.
The research role resolves to google_free primary, nim fallback, then the paid ovh fallback which is still declared but ineligible at zero cost.
The architect role resolves to nim minimax-m3 primary then nim and zai fallbacks; the primary has no alias and keeps its declared model id.
The tests role maps groq qwen3.6-27b through its certified replacement alias qwen/qwen3.8-27b rather than the deprecated id.
The review role declares four candidates and its last one, mistral, is paid and therefore not free-eligible at the configured zero budget.
The security role resolves to nim nemotron-3-ultra primary then zai.
The vision_qa role resolves to google_free gemini-flash then the free openrouter vision fallback.
The summarise role resolves to groq gpt-oss-20b then google_free gemini-flash-lite, giving the fallback proof two distinct providers.
The router role resolves to three candidates so a router decision can itself fail over deterministically.
embeddings is a configured role for local fastembed but is deliberately not a client-visible logical model; configuration is not exposure.

Every logical model the boundary advertises to clients resolves to at least one configured candidate. An advertised-but-unconfigured model would be accepted from a client and then fail to route, which reads as an outage rather than a configuration defect. Configured-but-unadvertised roles such as embeddings are reported and are deliberately not a violation.
A valid logical role is accepted, resolves to itself, and carries the pinned deterministic temperature of 0.
An unknown model is refused with 400 model_not_found at the boundary and is unroutable by the control plane.
A physical model id is refused: clients select logical roles, and a physical model is never a client-selectable model name.
An empty model is refused with 400 invalid_type rather than defaulting to any role.
A role that exists in models.yaml is refused at the boundary because it is not advertised as a client-visible logical model.
An unknown request field naming a provider is rejected, not ignored, so a client cannot steer physical provider selection.
A client cannot select a lane; without this rejection a client could attempt to request the restricted lane.
A provider base_url field is rejected so a client cannot redirect inference to an endpoint outside Company OS policy.

The restricted lane is declared and denies automation, the boundary default lane is internal, and no request field can select a lane, so the restricted lane is unreachable from an automated agent surface.
deny_all_automation denies every provider Company OS can name, including local, so no provider can serve the restricted lane automatically.
The internal lane permits exactly the six declared providers and denies local, mistral and ovh.
The confidential lane denies the free inference providers named in its deny list and permits local explicitly.
The public lane permits exactly the six declared providers and denies local, mistral and ovh.
nim is a declared free provider, so it is allowed at a zero cost budget.
ovh is neither a free provider nor free by model, and max_cost_usd is 0, so the paid candidate is blocked rather than silently used.
mistral is paid and its free entitlement is not verified, so it is blocked on the entitlement reason rather than on generic cost.
The local provider is free-eligible by rule, so the embedding primary is allowed at a zero cost budget.
A reviewer resolving to the implementer's own vendor is denied reviewer independence.
A reviewer on a different vendor from the implementer is allowed.
Separation compares resolved vendors, so nim is denied against implementer vendor nvidia even though the provider names differ.
Vendor separation constrains review only; the implement role is exempt even when its vendor matches.
The primary candidate serves the request on the first attempt with no fallback and no retry.
rate_limited yields exactly four retries on the same candidate before deterministic fallback to the next candidate.
transient yields exactly two retries, fewer than rate_limited, then falls over to the next candidate.
When every candidate exhausts its retries the router fails closed with no_eligible_provider rather than returning an unproven result.
Every candidate is blocked by lane policy before any provider is contacted, so the restricted lane reaches no provider even when all providers would otherwise succeed.
A candidate at or below the low quota threshold is down-ranked, so the fallback is preferred while the primary is still callable.
A pinned candidate makes one attempt with no retry and no fallback, so certification cannot be masked by a healthy fallback.
Pinning a candidate that is not configured for the role fails closed with candidate_not_found and contacts no provider.
The reviewer candidate on the implementer's vendor is blocked by policy and the next candidate serves the request.
A router response satisfying the decision contract is reduced to a validated decision rather than relayed as provider prose.

cases.justification: The operator CLI refuses the restricted lane with exit 2 and contacts no provider, matching the lane policy the router would apply.
The CLI surfaces candidate_not_found with exit 1 rather than silently falling back to a different candidate.
The CLI enforces reviewer vendor separation and serves the request from a different vendor.
The CLI constrains lane selection to the four declared lanes and rejects anything else before any routing occurs.
The client sees the logical role it requested; neither the physical provider nor the physical model appears in the completion.
Provider reasoning fields are stripped at the control-plane edge and are not relayed to the client, and the provider system fingerprint is not exposed.
